e7_s4_rationale: The presence of a submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration of the overlying mucosa and a well-defined, heterogeneous, pre-pyloric mass with fat attenuation on CT is most consistent with a gastrointestinal stromal tumor, especially given the lack of malignant features on biopsy which might have suggested gastric adenocarcinoma.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Peptic ulcer disease
e7_s4_rejected.why: While peptic ulcer disease could cause epigastric pain and hematemesis, the presence of a submucosal lesion and a well-defined mass is not typical for peptic ulcers.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Gastric adenocarcinoma
e7_s4_rejected.why: The biopsy showed no malignant features, making gastric adenocarcinoma less likely.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Dieulafoy's lesion
e7_s4_rejected.why: Dieulafoy's lesion typically presents with a small, bleeding mucosal defect over a large, tortuous artery, which does not match the description of a submucosal lesion with a well-defined mass.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Lipoma
e7_s4_rejected.why: While lipomas can be submucosal and have fat attenuation on CT, they are typically not associated with ulceration of the overlying mucosa or significant bleeding as seen in this patient.

B06_pred: Gastric gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST); Gastric lipoma
